text:
Zoe Kim: Heads-up on a weird onboarding issue with the new monorepo-next-starter that wires LlamaIndex embeddings + shared cache. After deploying, some tenants see 401s and stale embeddings returned. Repro steps attached. cc @Harpreet

Zoe Kim: Repro (very small):
```js
// apps/customer-a/pages/api/embed.js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js'
const client = createClient(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
const cache = require('../../../../shared/emb-cache') // singleton store in monorepo
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const key = req.body.text
  const cached = cache.get(key)
  if (cached) return res.json(cached)
  const out = await client.embed({ model: 'redwood/mini', input: key })
  cache.set(key, out)
  res.json(out)
}
```

Harpreet Singh: Important context: the monorepo starter runs multiple Next apps in the same serverless deployment during dev/staging. If infra rotates staging keys, the module-scoped client instance in shared packages may be stale. Also, the emb-cache is shared across tenants so stale/unauth'd responses can leak between apps.

Marco Alvarez: I repro'd locally by toggling a short-lived key. When upstream returns 401 with x-rw-exp header the SDK treats it as terminal and returns the 401 payload which we then cache. So subsequent requests serve cached 401 body as embedding blob -> broken UX. That's nasty.

Elaine Cho: Oof. Two issues to fix: (1) SDK should not surface 401 bodies as successful results to callers (should throw and allow callers to avoid caching). (2) Starter guidance: don't cache raw responses without verifying status; add a helper that only caches on 2xx.

Zoe Kim: Agreed. Quick patch in the starter: wrap client call and check for .status >=200 && <300 before cache.set. But still want SDK parity fix so JS client mirrors Python's rotation/refresh behavior.

Harpreet Singh: SDK change proposal: on auth error (401) if response contains x-rw-exp <= now + 20s, do a single auth refresh and retry. Also ensure streaming/embedding flows throw an Error object (not a 200 payload) so callers can't accidentally cache error bodies.

Marco Alvarez: I'll open a PR implementing both server-side guard (only cache on success) in the starter and a small change in SDK: never treat 401 as success, and expose a helper isRetryableAuth(err, headers). Add unit tests that assert we don't cache 401 payloads.

Elaine Cho: Also add an e2e that simulates short-lived keys and asserts that embeddings returned after rotation are valid and that no tenant leaks occur. Add a CI smoke job to run the monorepo starter scenario.

Dev CI Bot: workflow/devex-monorepo-smoke triggered for branch fix/emb-cache-auth-guard (1/1) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Harpreet Singh: One more nuance: shared in-memory cache in monorepos isn't safe for multi-app deployments in serverless; recommend starter to include adapter examples (local-memory for dev, Redis for prod) and a note to namespace caches by tenant to avoid cross-tenant leakage. I'll update the README.

Zoe Kim: Thanks. I'll patch the starter example to namespace keys with a tenant id and gate caching behind status checks. Will re-run onboarding after CI.

Marco Alvarez: Draft SDK PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/901  adds auth-refresh-on-rotation + ensures non-2xx responses throw. Includes unit + e2e sim.

Elaine Cho: Assigning ticket DX-MONO-77 to Marco+Harpreet for SDK fix, starter guard, tests, and README updates.

Zoe Kim: Verified staging after merge: no more cached 401s, tenants isolated, onboarding passes. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
